references.text: Jesus states the same paradox in another context: 'Whoever finds their life will lose it, and whoever loses their life for my sake will find it' ([ref:Matt 10:39|Matthew 10:39]). This is a parallel formulation of the principle that whoever seeks to preserve their life will lose it.

Jesus says: 'For whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake will find it' ([ref:Matt 16:25|Matthew 16:25]). The same fundamental paradox about losing and finding life.

Mark's parallel: 'For whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake and for the gospel's sake will save it' ([ref:Mark 8:35|Mark 8:35]). Identical theme of self-sacrifice versus self-preservation.

An earlier occurrence of the same statement in Luke: 'For whoever wants to save their life will lose it. But whoever loses their life for my sake, they will save it' ([ref:Luk 9:24|Luke 9:24]). Luke presents this principle twice in his gospel.

Jesus says: 'Whoever loves their life will lose it. But whoever hates their life in this world will keep it and gain eternal life' ([ref:Joh 12:25|John 12:25]). John uses the image of the grain of wheat that must die to bear fruit, linking it to the same paradox of losing and keeping life.

Lot's wife looked back toward Sodom and became a pillar of salt ([ref:1 Mos 19:17-26|Genesis 19:17-26]). The context in Luke 17 explicitly mentions Lot's wife (v. 32) as a warning example of someone who sought to hold on to what they had, and thus lost their life.

Paul counted everything he once considered gain as loss for the sake of Christ ([ref:Fil 3:7-8|Philippians 3:7-8]). This illustrates the principle of letting go of everything to win Christ – to 'lose' one's life in order to find true life.

Some were tortured and refused to accept release, so that they might gain a better resurrection ([ref:Hebr 11:35|Hebrews 11:35]). The witnesses of faith were willing to lose their earthly lives to gain the eternal – a concrete fulfillment of Jesus' words in Luke 17:33.
